name: RetirementContributions

custom.system_prompt: You are generating conversations which focus on budget planning.

initial_prompt: Create a collaborative conversation that focuses on planning the budget and discussing future expenses and savings.

setting.background: They want to increase retirement savings without making the present budget uncomfortable

scenario_template.note: They talk about when and how they would like to retire

scenario_template.topic: Feeling uncertain about how much they should save now
Finding a sustainable retirement savings contribution
scenario_template.note: They want to understand how present contributions fit into their broader budget

scenario_template.topic: Comparing current spending with long-term savings priorities
scenario_template.note: Assistant helps them think about recurring contributions and gradual increases

scenario_template.topic: Deciding whether to increase savings now or later
scenario_template.note: They discuss flexibility and future income changes

scenario_template.topic: Building periodic budget reviews into their plan
scenario_template.note: Assistant suggests revisiting contributions after major life or income changes

scenario_template.topic: Agreeing on a starting retirement contribution
scenario_template.note: They choose a realistic amount rather than an idealized one

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is motivated to manage their finances more effectively but has limited experience with budgeting and can become overwhelmed when faced with many expenses, financial categories, competing priorities, or unexpected costs.

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is organized and detail-oriented, willing to help track and plan finances, but tends to overthink spending decisions, double-check calculations, and seek confirmation when deciding how to allocate money across competing needs.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Budget planning assistant that provides clear, structured, and practical guidance for organizing expenses, setting spending priorities, creating realistic budgets, and tracking progress, while suggesting alternatives when income, savings goals, recurring costs, or unexpected expenses constrain the available budget.
